text: Mantra is a technique and not the goal. When you feel you have entered a deep state and chanting the mantra also takes effort, Stop! But watch out, the mind is very tricky, it may be laziness which may be preventing you from chanting. So, examine carefully.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti. Without the havan kund, no homa can be done.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana, the Supreme energy. In yogic terms, it is the movement of the aspiration, thought, concentration and energy towards either the higher side or the lower side. When it goes down it leads to material wellbeing. When it goes up, it leads to Spiritual wellbeing.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: We have the most complex brain, better than any other animals therefore we tend to think that it is because of this that everything is functioning. Consciousness can be totally free of the brain and act on its own if required.
author: Sri M

text: Be a bhakta - devotee more than anything else because through bhakti all jnana - wisdom will dawn.
author: Sri M

text: When you have gone deep enough in your meditation, in your spiritual practice, you are not aware of the outside world in a state of deep trance, you are not even thinking of any idea what you should do or what you should not do, suddenly a thought will come into your mind. You may not even have thought about it and it's not even from your subconscious. It comes deep from within and then you know, yes, this is to be done, then it's your inner Guru speaking. It may not even be speaking in words. It may be suddenly that you realize, I know this.
author: Sri M

text: As you journey on the path, the more you desire, the more is your aspiration towards having a glimpse of the Supreme, then something very soft and nice grows in your heart. It's very fragrant. And when it grows, that is devotion.
author: Sri M

text: It is the function of the Outer Guru, a teacher, to bring about the development of the student so that he / she becomes more reliant on the Inner Guru than the Outer Guru. The Outer Guru can disappear, but the Inner does not. The Inner Guru is actually none other than the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the Guru is to show a mirror to you. To clean the mirror and show it properly at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be.
author: Sri M

text: When you say Guru, it means a teacher in all ways; could be a small child who teaches you innocence of childhood, it could be a philosophical teacher who teaches you the Upanishads, they are all Gurus.
author: Sri M

text: Following the teachings is more important than worshipping the Teacher.
author: Sri M

text: When the ordinary thinking or the ordinary rational logic subsides, then comes the feeling called Bhakti. Bhakti is not different from Jnana Yoga but it’s that which comes with feelings not words, sound or music.
author: Sri M

text: When you live in this world be aware of how you behave. Be mindful of what you do in the outside world, be mindful of your inner world and one day what will remain is only the witness, the sakshi which is the seer. This is kaivalya.
author: Sri M

text: Because you are emotional, it doesn’t mean that you should not maintain tranquility. Your emotions should be directed towards achieving your goal, rather than in other things.
author: Sri M

text: Half an hour or one hour of sitting down quietly and being mindful of your mind, thoughts and breath is a very important preparation to attain that mindfulness which we seek, which is to be totally free of all this.
author: Sri M

text: In life we go through all circumstances. Sometimes there is happiness, sometimes there is sorrow. Sometimes people blame you, sometimes they praise you. The yogi is one who considers praise and blame as equal. He is not moved by it.
author: Sri M

text: There are some people who seem to be happy in all situations because they have found out through experiences of life that the peace, tranquility and happiness that they seek is inside, not outside.
author: Sri M

text: Don't be obsessed with failure. All people who have succeeded are those who have failed and continued and said we will somehow do it.
author: Sri M

text: There is a divinity in every heart, and that divinity - by its very essence - is peace, tranquility, and happiness. The more you tune into it, the happier you are, the better your mind is, and the better you function in your relationship with others.
author: Sri M

text: Layers of prejudice close the eyes, ears, and heart. When the wind blows, nothing can enter. So, all the practices we do are meant to open the windows to the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever happens, even if you are sick, try not to miss the routine practice of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Bhajan is not just chanting or singing. It means to completely absorb yourself in the Inner. It is actually a spiritual version of bhojan for the physical body. So it is a bhojan for the mind.
author: Sri M

text: The evolved human being is not judged by the number of cars he owns or the dollars in his bank balance. The hallmark of an evolved being is the quality of his heart - love, understanding and a strong desire for peace.
author: Sri M

text: A person whose mind is completely and totally on the path, he will do only what is right and forget about the rest! But it is not so easy. It can come only with spiritual maturity.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes it is difficult for us to distinguish what is real and what is unreal. For that, we need maximum alertness, which develops as part of our sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion is spontaneous. We can teach all the ways leading to it but what it is, can’t be taught. Suddenly, the seed sprouts; we don’t know how. It sprouts in different ways for different people.
author: Sri M
